summary: This Dockerfile creates a lightweight Docker image running a FastAPI web application. It starts with a minimal Python environment, installs the FastAPI framework, copies your application code into the container, and then runs a development server that automatically restarts whenever your code changes.

explanations.2: We're using the 'slim' variant of Python, which is a much smaller download than the standard Python image but still has everything needed to run Python code.
explanations.5: This sets /app as the working directory, meaning all file operations inside the container will happen relative to this folder, like how 'cd /app' would work on your computer.
explanations.8: We're installing FastAPI and its standard dependencies (the '[standard]' part) before copying our code, so if the code changes later, we don't have to reinstall everything.
explanations.11: We copy main.py from your computer into the container at the same location (also called main.py), making your application code available inside the container.
explanations.16: We start the Uvicorn server (which runs FastAPI apps) with --reload enabled, meaning if you change main.py, the server automatically restarts and reloads the changes without you having to manually restart it.
